subject: BrightWave MAP: onboarding checklist and peering options
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Turner <amy@brightwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightWave MAP: onboarding checklist and peering options

Hi Amy —

Following our call this morning, I attached an initial MAP worksheet (BrightWave_MAP_v1.xlsx) with the onboarding milestones we discussed. Items I flagged as blockers for a trial:

- Org & tenant creation (workspace+billing contact)
- API key provisioning (ephemeral and long-lived options)
- IP allowlist for our hosted endpoints (you provided ranges on call)
- VPC peering option for Dedicated/Private (if your infra team prefers peering over NAT)

Quick asks to keep this sprint tight:
1) Can you confirm the BrightWave IT contact for peering (email + preferred CIDR ranges)?
2) Do you want us to provision ephemeral API keys scoped to the trial environment, or will you manage keys from your side?
3) Target close date — you mentioned mid-next-week on the call; is Friday 5/21 realistic?

Marissa (CC) will lead the tech checklist; she’ll follow up with a short runbook and VPC diagram. I’ll send the DocuSign SOW for signatures once we lock the timeline.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.ai

Alex —

Thanks for the summary and the MAP draft. Quick answers from our side:

- IT contact for peering: Jordan Lee (jordan.lee@brightwave.com). Please loop him in for the VPC CIDR validation.
- CIDR ranges we can allocate for peering: 10.40.0.0/16 and 10.41.0.0/16.
- On keys: we'd prefer Redwood to provision ephemeral keys scoped to the trial; our security team will rotate keys on our side if long-lived keys are needed later.
- Timeline: trying for Friday 5/21 would be great — Jordan needs to confirm peering windows but should be able to prioritize.

I copied Jordan into the thread (separate message to follow from him with availability).

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Amy Turner <amy@brightwave.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightWave MAP: onboarding checklist and peering options

Hi Amy, Alex —

Thanks for the details, Amy. I sketched a short technical runbook and attached a simple VPC diagram (vpc-config-diagram.png). Summary of the practical steps we suggest for the POC environment:

1) Organization setup
   - Alex to confirm billing owner (we can create the BrightWave tenant or accept your existing tenant ID).
   - Create a scoped eval workspace labeled "brightwave-trial-2027".

2) API keys
   - We will issue ephemeral API keys (30d TTL) scoped to the eval workspace.
   - If you want programmatic rotation, use the redwood-ephemeral-key-template.txt attached for automation.

3) IP allowlist
   - Please confirm public egress ranges (we'll add to our allowlist once confirmed by your IT).

4) VPC peering (optional but recommended for lower-latency private traffic)
   - If BrightWave wants peering, we'll exchange route targets and configure the peering session. Our networking team needs a single point of contact (Jordan) and a maintenance window (we typically prefer 2–4 hours).

Proposed sprint tasks for the next 72 hours:
- Day 0 (today): Alex confirms billing owner and workspace name.
- Day 1: We provision ephemeral keys and share them via secure link.
- Day 2: Jordan and our infra team complete CIDR validation and, if agreed, establish peering.

I attached the diagram and the quick key template. Let me know if you prefer a jump call to walk the infra team through the peering steps.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: vpc-config-diagram.png, redwood-ephemeral-key-template.txt

- Confirmed billing contact or tenant ID (so we can bind the eval workspace)

- A signed SOW (I've included a DocuSign link below for the small trial SOW).

DocuSign (trial SOW): https://www.docusign.com/link/ABCDEF-12345

Once those are in, we'll provision keys and seed the workspace. If Jordan prefers to skip peering for the initial trial, the test can still proceed over the public endpoints with the IP allowlist in place.
